quotes.text: A resource can run all day because planners keep feeding it work, even when the work leaving that resource can't become a finished, shippable product at the same rate.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why high machine utilization alone does not prove a capacity problem.

quotes.text: A strong OEE number doesn't tell you whether the plant has enough capacity for the demand mix and a weak OEE number doesn't prove you need more equipment either.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Draws a clear line between an equipment metric and an investment decision.

quotes.text: Data tells you that a machine stopped. Context tells you which orders, routes, tools, people, and customer commitments that stop can affect.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the difference between reporting an event and reasoning about a decision.

quotes.text: Simulation lets you test decisions without using customer delivery as the test environment. It isn't a factory animation.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the real purpose of simulation in two short sentences.

quotes.text: Microsoft Fabric doesn't replace an MES that manages execution and traceability. It doesn't automatically create finite schedules that respect every setup, skill, fixture, and routing rule.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sets a clear architecture boundary for what a data platform does and does not do.

chapters.title: Machine problem or production system problem?
Experiments: machine, shifts, release rules, routing

takeaways: High utilization at one machine does not prove that a second machine will increase shipped output; the constraint often moves downstream.
Discrete event simulation lets you compare a machine purchase with shift changes, release rules, batch sizes and routing rules before committing capital.
Microsoft Fabric, Power BI and Azure provide the governed data layer, but ERP, MES and specialized scheduling and simulation logic still own planning and execution.
hook: Your busiest machine has a growing queue and someone wants to buy another one. This episode is for manufacturing leaders, planners and finance teams who need to know whether they face a machine capacity problem or a production system problem. You will learn how to test the purchase against shift, release, batch and routing alternatives with simulation and a governed data foundation.
